lens: Linus — taste, simplicity, kill ceremony, prefer deletion
answer: Reviewed at merge commit 70b83631. The mechanical part of this PR is fine taste: `git mv` (history-preserving), all 7 inbound refs across 5 files rewritten consistently (kernel lib.rs:83/247/321, app main.rs:38 ARGO_MANIFEST, three evidence JSONs), Argo's self-referential `spec.source.path` inside application.json also rewritten so the manifest still resolves itself. Net diff is +85/-139 — deletion-dominant, exactly what Linus likes. `.audit/agent-read.jsonl` (130 lines of agent-read telemetry) deleted from tracking with `.gitignore` add — correct, that file never belonged in git. `.config/nextest.toml` correctly kept tracked because CI consumes `[profile.ci]` (this was the merge-block on a prior attempt). Good engineering. The Linus complaint is the ceremony around it: a 73-line ADR (ADR-0117) for what is, structurally, `git mv` + two lines in `.gitignore`. The ADR even has a dedicated 'Naming justification' section that says 'the move is path-only, no crate or capability naming changes' — i.e., it justifies that no justification is needed. That is exactly the compliance theater Linus would mock. The repo policy (`feedback_naming_justification`) forces it, so the engineer is not to blame; the policy is the smell. Second taste issue: bundling two unrelated changes (gitignore audit log + kyverno consolidation) in one PR violates 'one logical change per commit'. The PR body itself admits 'two unrelated low-risk fixes'. If either had to be reverted, you cannot revert one without the other. That is bad hygiene, ironic in a hygiene PR. Third taste issue: ADR-0117's 'Naming justification' asserts `infra/kyverno/` is the established admission-policy root WITHOUT citing ADR-0039/0041/0052 that actually establish it (already flagged by A3 sibling) — the kind of self-evident assertion Linus calls 'because I said so'. Net Linus verdict: the change pulls its weight (deletion-dominant, fixes a real CI/sprawl problem), but it is wrapped in more ceremony than the substance deserves and bundles two changes. Approve-with-fixups — the fixups land on POLICY (loosen the ADR-for-everything rule for CC-2 hygiene; enforce one-logical-change-per-PR), not on this PR which is already merged.
key_claims: git mv preserves history; all 7 inbound refs across 5 files rewritten consistently to infra/kyverno/oya-vcs-admission at merge commit 70b83631
Argo's self-referential spec.source.path inside application.json was rewritten — without this, the moved manifest would still point Argo at the old (now nonexistent) repo path
Net diff is +85/-139 — deletion-dominant, which is the right shape for a hygiene PR
.audit/agent-read.jsonl (130 lines of agent-read telemetry) correctly untracked + .gitignore'd; never belonged in version control
.config/nextest.toml correctly kept tracked because CI sets NEXTEST_PROFILE=ci and requires [profile.ci] — earlier untrack attempt broke the merge queue, this PR fixed that
Two unrelated changes (gitignore audit log + kyverno consolidation) bundled into one PR violates the one-logical-change-per-PR rule; the PR body itself admits 'two unrelated low-risk fixes'
ADR-0117 is 73 lines documenting what is structurally `git mv` + two lines of .gitignore — disproportionate ceremony for the substance

The 'Naming justification' section literally states 'the move is path-only, no crate or capability naming changes' i.e., justifies that no justification is needed — compliance theater forced by the naming-justification doctrine
ADR-0117 §'Naming justification' asserts `infra/kyverno/` is the established admission-policy root WITHOUT citing ADR-0039/0041/0052 that actually establish it — assertion-not-citation
uncertainty_areas: Whether any out-of-repo Argo ApplicationSet, Flux Kustomization, or cluster-side automation hardcodes the old deploy/gitops/oya-vcs-admission path — only in-repo references were verified

Whether the .audit/agent-read.jsonl content scrubbed from HEAD remains in git history across prior commits (rm --cached does not rewrite history); F7 sibling reviewer notes it does, with low-sensitivity content (path arguments to git log/read, no credentials)
Whether the one-logical-change rule is encoded as a CI lane or only as informal doctrine in this repo — if not encoded, the bundling fixup has no enforcement teeth
anti_patterns_detected: compliance-theater-naming-justification: ADR-0117 has a dedicated 'Naming justification' section whose content is 'no naming changes occurred', forced by the feedback_naming_justification doctrine
bundled-unrelated-changes: PR explicitly admits two unrelated fixes in one PR; bisect/revert granularity destroyed
ADR-for-mechanical-rename: 73-line Accepted ADR (with deciders + status + supersedes/superseded_by + related) for a `git mv` + 2-line .gitignore — disproportionate ceremony
assertion-not-citation: 'infra/kyverno/ is the established admission-policy root' stated as self-evident without citing ADR-0039/0041/0052
doc-source-of-truth-drift: docs/DESIGN.md §8 still lists deploy/ as a canonical top-level dir (per A3 sibling) — the PR removed deploy/ but did not update DESIGN.md, creating a fresh inconsistency

findings.summary: Bundled two unrelated changes (.audit/.gitignore + kyverno consolidation) in one PR; revert granularity destroyed. PR body explicitly admits this.
findings.recommended_action: Future hygiene PRs: one logical change per PR. Enforce via PR-template checklist or a lane that fails when multiple top-level scopes are touched without a single shared subject.

findings.summary: ADR-0117 is 73 lines of ceremony for `git mv` + 2 lines of .gitignore. The 'Naming justification' section literally justifies that no justification is needed.
findings.recommended_action: Loosen the ADR-for-everything doctrine for CC-2 path-only/hygiene changes: a one-paragraph PR-body justification + commit-message citation should suffice without a full ADR document. Amend feedback_naming_justification + the ADR template to exempt CC-2 mechanical renames.

findings.summary: ADR-0117 §'Naming justification' asserts `infra/kyverno/` is the canonical admission-policy root without citing ADR-0039/0041/0052 that actually establish it.
findings.recommended_action: Add citations to ADR-0039 (lines 104-108), ADR-0041 (lines 117-118/135), ADR-0052 (line 189) in ADR-0117's 'Naming justification' section. Follow-up amendment-PR or supersede with ADR-0117a.

findings.summary: docs/DESIGN.md §8 'The flat target shape' still lists `deploy/` as a canonical top-level directory after PR-12 removed it. Fresh doc-source-of-truth drift introduced by this PR.
findings.recommended_action: Follow-up PR amending DESIGN.md §8 to remove `deploy/` from the canonical top-level list; ideally a CI lane (doc-shape-vs-tree) that fails when DESIGN.md's directory enumeration disagrees with the actual repo tree.
